records.Concise description: Foundry Digital’s institutional Bitcoin mining pool, using an FPPS payout model and globally distributed Stratum infrastructure.
records.Deeper researched summary: Foundry USA Pool coordinates hashers that connect to its pool endpoints; it does not own all hashrate pointed at it. Its current product materials describe an FPPS model, in which the pool operator assumes block-discovery variance and pays participating miners according to accepted work, including a modeled transaction-fee component. Foundry’s current pool positioning emphasizes institutional onboarding, compliance, monitoring, and globally distributed relay infrastructure.
records.Launch / history: Launched in 2020 by Foundry Digital and grew into a major Bitcoin mining pool during the 2021–2026 period.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin mining eco: A durable example of an institutional-scale shared pool and FPPS risk-transfer model. It is useful for explaining the difference between independent hashers, a pool coordinator, estimated pool block share, and pool-owned hardware.
Important technical or cultural characte: Pool operator bears short-run block variance
Pool block share is an estimate, not owned network hashrate
records.Verification basis: Current Foundry-controlled pool materials verify the operator, active service, Bitcoin pool role, and FPPS model.
Research notes / uncertainties: Do not publish current pool hashrate or network-share percentages as durable facts; they change continuously.
Pool coordination must not be described as ownership of all participating hashrate.

records.Concise description: A large multi-coin mining pool launched by BITMAIN in 2014 and operated independently from BITMAIN since its 2021 spin-off.
records.Deeper researched summary: AntPool currently offers Bitcoin mining with pooled payout options including FPPS and PPLNS. BITMAIN’s own company history states that AntPool was launched by BITMAIN in 2014 and was spun off as an independent entity in May 2021, so MSC should preserve the historical relationship without treating AntPool as a currently BITMAIN-owned pool unless stronger current corporate evidence says otherwise.
Creators / founders: BITMAIN — original launcher; spun AntPool off in May 2021
records.Launch / history: BITMAIN launched AntPool in 2014; BITMAIN states that AntPool became independent in May 2021.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin mining eco: AntPool is both historically significant to ASIC-era pool concentration and still operational. It also illustrates why manufacturer, pool, and hasher identities must be modeled separately.
Important technical or cultural characte: Historical BITMAIN lineage but post-2021 independence
Pool-policy layer distinct from Bitcoin consensus
records.Verification basis: Current AntPool service materials plus BITMAIN’s first-party corporate history verify active operation and the 2014 launch / 2021 spin-off relationship.
Research notes / uncertainties: Do not describe AntPool as currently owned by BITMAIN based only on its launch history.
Fee schedules and payout thresholds are time-sensitive and should be dated if later used in public copy.

records.Concise description: ViaBTC’s long-running Bitcoin mining pool, launched in 2016 and offering PPS+, PPLNS, and solo-style payout options.
records.Deeper researched summary: ViaBTC launched its Bitcoin pool in June 2016 and currently documents multiple payout modes. Its PPS+ model combines a pay-per-share subsidy component with transaction-fee allocation, while PPLNS exposes miners to more pool luck/variance and its SOLO mode pays only when the participating miner finds a block under the service’s rules. ViaBTC also documents merged-mining rewards for selected auxiliary chains.
records.Launch / history: ViaBTC’s official history dates its pool launch to June 5, 2016.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin mining eco: It is a durable shared-pool example with multiple payout models under one operator and is useful for teaching that payout accounting can differ even when miners contribute the same proof-of-work shares.
Important technical or cultural characte: Payout model changes miner variance and pool risk, not Bitcoin consensus
records.Verification basis: Current ViaBTC-controlled website/support materials verify active operation, launch history, supported Bitcoin mining, and documented payout choices.
Research notes / uncertainties: Do not infer Stratum V2 support without a current first-party source.
Fee percentages and minimum payouts are time-sensitive.

records.Concise description: One of Bitcoin’s longest-running large mining pools, founded in 2013 and currently offering Bitcoin pool mining with FPPS and PPLNS options.
records.Deeper researched summary: F2Pool began in 2013 and remains an active mining pool. Its current Bitcoin support material documents pooled mining endpoints, payment configuration, and current payout options. As with other pools, observed block share is only a rolling estimate of work coordinated through the service and should not be equated with permanently controlled network hashrate.
records.Launch / history: Founded in 2013; F2Pool’s own history materials identify it as one of the earliest surviving large mining pools.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin mining eco: Its longevity makes it a useful bridge between early pooled mining and the modern industrial mining era.
Important technical or cultural characte: Merged-mining rewards supported for some auxiliary chains
records.Verification basis: Current F2Pool-controlled service/support materials verify active Bitcoin pool operation and payout model choices; first-party history materials support its 2013 lineage.
Research notes / uncertainties: Do not freeze current hashrate, fee, or payout-threshold values into timeless public copy.
